title: Keep supervising the shell through a slow compositor resume
head: d4b4b7596206
workflow: Opus full review, Sol boundary hunter, Opus self-check of the draft, editorial check, batch gates

leads.summary: A stop signal during the new wait gets journaled as compositor failure
leads.consequence: The TERM/HUP/INT trap sets terminating=1. The new loop returns failure when it sees this flag, and the caller logs 'the compositor stopped answering' unconditionally before exiting zero. A deliberate session teardown therefore generates misleading crash diagnostics even if the IPC socket is still bound. When the compositor starts answering just as TERM arrives, the loop can instead return success and log 'relaunching' while the top-level terminating check prevents any relaunch. Recheck terminating after compositor_alive before either logger (and immediately after sleep if prompt teardown is desired).

leads.summary: Socket-bind failure silently drops the only slow-resume test against current quattro's skip reporting
leads.consequence: When python3 is unavailable or bind fails, socket_bound=0 and the only slow-resume assertion is simply omitted. No SKIP line is printed, and current quattro's runner treats the file as all tests passed, concealing lost coverage. Call skip with a reason in the else path, as test/shell.d/compositor-guard-test.sh does in the tip, while preserving the unconditional no-socket checks.

leads.summary: Related PR #10709 merges textually but makes this PR's new slow-resume test fail
leads.consequence: #10709 intentionally relaunches unexpected clean exits instead of stopping at status 0. This PR's new case uses statuses $'255\n0' and expects launch_shell to return success, so after #10709 the second shell's clean exit keeps relaunching until its attempt budget fails or timeout 30 interrupts the run. Change that test to $'255\nrun' and stop the launcher explicitly, as #10709 does for its modeset test. Its new no-socket test retains an immediate exit because compositor_alive fails.
leads.triage: behavioural; Opus followup Q3 confirmed combined #10709 tree fails slow-resume case (fixture assumption); adapted case passes

leads.summary: PR #13490's instance-adoption guard overlaps this PR's compositor guard and needs a semantic merge
leads.consequence: Both change compositor_alive and introduce helpers at the same point. A three-way merge has conflict markers around the helper declarations and guard body. More importantly, blindly retaining #13490's first ten adopt_live_instance retries but appending this PR's extra wait yields 60 further hyprctl monitors calls pinned to the inherited (possibly crashed) signature, without any further adoption attempts. If a watchdog replacement comes up after those first retries while the old IPC socket remains, the supervisor will wait and then give up rather than adopting the replacement. Resolve with one consistent adopt/retry strategy, not simply both guards in series.

leads.summary: No-socket test only removes the signature, leaving a bound socket; it misses a broken socket predicate
leads.consequence: The test never removes the bound socket and calls launch_shell with its fourth argument unset, so the predicate short-circuits on empty signature. Replacing the production -S test with '[[ -n $signature ]]' passes every head test but would wait through a dead compositor whenever a real, nonempty signature outlives a removed socket. Add a case with a nonempty signature and no socket or a removed socket at that signature, and assert immediate stand-down and logger output.
leads.triage: factual check by coordinator (test line 170 passes empty signature); Opus followup Q1 confirmed mutant survives and fix

leads.summary: The 12-miss test does not protect the reported 26-second recovery window
leads.consequence: Only nine of the 12 missed queries occur in the added loop. Cutting the maximum from 60 to 20 half-second polls still passes the whole test file, although that implementation gives up before the issue's approximately 26-second resume. A >26-second recovery case needs a timeout larger than the existing 30 seconds plus launcher startup and relaunch slack, or a deterministic time-controlled fixture.
leads.triage: Opus followup Q2 confirmed bound 10 passes; stubbed-sleep case guards it

leads.summary: The promised 30-second guard is not a wall-clock limit if hyprctl connects but stops receiving replies
leads.consequence: Each of up to 63 sequential hyprctl requests may block on its IPC receive timeout (5 seconds at Hyprland v0.56.2), in addition to the half-second sleeps. The shell may stand down and a trapped signal may be observed much later than claimed, even while the socket exists. The fixture's hyprctl stub exits immediately, so tests do not cover this dependency behavior. Bound elapsed time and/or individual IPC calls if 'up to 30 more seconds' and timely teardown are contract requirements.

limits: Per assignment boundary no live compositor, suspend, session lock, or host logger/journal was used; observations are read-only source and isolated fixture results.

comment:
## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Outcome:** The change is not shown to fix #11820, which `Fixes` would close.

### `Fixes #11820` is not established

On Hyprland 0.56.2, `hyprctl -j monitors` exits 0 with `[]` when there are no outputs, so a blackout alone does not trip `compositor_alive`. The base guard stands down on a connect failure or ~16 s of stalled IPC, and the issue's log of a resume the shell survived shows IPC events 3 s in. **Impact:** the issue would close on a hypothesis.

**Suggested change:** use `Refs #11820` until the new journal line confirms this path.

<details><summary>Evidence (hyprctl probe, not a failing test)</summary>

Sources, Hyprland v0.56.2:
- `src/debug/HyprCtl.cpp:313-343`: `monitorsRequest` builds `[` + entries + `]`, so no monitors gives `[]`.
- `hyprctl/src/main.cpp:201-281`: with the signature set, exit 4 on connect failure, 5 on write failure, 6 on a read failure or the 5 s receive timeout, 7 on an `error:` reply; otherwise 0.
- The issue's `quickshell.hyprland.ipc: Got removal for monitor "FALLBACK"` at 15:02:04 (from a resume the shell survived; the issue says that resume shows the same churn and 26 s gap) is logged when Quickshell 0.3.1 reads a `monitorremoved` event from `.socket2.sock`. Hyprland writes those events from the same event loop that serves `.socket.sock`.
- When a lock client disconnects, Hyprland stays locked and draws its own lock-dead screen (`src/render/Renderer.cpp:1676-1683`), not the client's last frame. The issue reports the password box still visible.

Hypothesis, not reproduced: a shell that hung but did not exit would match the report too. In that case the launcher is still in `wait`, logs nothing, and this PR does not change the outcome. On the next occurrence, the new journal line (or its absence) and, from a TTY, `pgrep -af 'quickshell|omarchy-launch-shell'` would settle it. The PR still helps when Hyprland keeps its socket but stops serving IPC.

**Probe of `hyprctl` answers:**

Needs `python3` and `hyprctl` (run here with hyprland 0.56.2-2). It uses a private `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` and stand-in sockets, never the running session.

The first stand-in replies `[]`, which is what Hyprland 0.56.2 sends for `j/monitors` when it has no monitors (`monitorsRequest` in `src/debug/HyprCtl.cpp` builds `[` + entries + `]`). Once the signature is set, `hyprctl` (`request()` in `hyprctl/src/main.cpp`) exits 0 unless the connect fails (4), the write fails (5), the read fails or times out after 5 s (6), or the reply starts with `error:` (7).

```bash
#!/bin/bash
# How `hyprctl -j monitors` answers for three compositor states, using a private
# runtime dir and stand-in sockets (never the running session).
# Needs python3 and hyprctl.
set -u
rt=$(mktemp -d)
sig=review_0_0
mkdir -p "$rt/hypr/$sig"
sock="$rt/hypr/$sig/.socket.sock"

ask() {
  local start end rc
  start=$(date +%s.%N)
  XDG_RUNTIME_DIR="$rt" HYPRLAND_INSTANCE_SIGNATURE="$sig" hyprctl -j monitors >"$rt/out" 2>&1
  rc=$?
  end=$(date +%s.%N)
  printf '%-40s exit %s after %.1fs: %s\n' "$1" "$rc" "$(awk -v a="$start" -v b="$end" 'BEGIN { print b - a }')" "$(tr '\n' ' ' <"$rt/out")"
}

serve() {  # $1 = answer: reply "[]" to one request; stall: listen, never accept
  rm -f "$sock" "$rt/ready"
  python3 -c '
import socket, sys, time
s = socket.socket(socket.AF_UNIX)
s.bind(sys.argv[1])
s.listen(10)
open(sys.argv[2], "w").write("ready")
if sys.argv[3] == "answer":
    c, _ = s.accept()
    c.recv(8192)
    c.sendall(b"[]")
    c.close()
else:
    time.sleep(60)
' "$sock" "$rt/ready" "$1" &
  server=$!
  until [[ -f $rt/ready ]]; do sleep 0.05; done
}

serve answer
ask "live compositor, every output gone:"
wait "$server"

serve stall
ask "live compositor, event loop stalled:"
kill "$server"; wait "$server" 2>/dev/null

rm -f "$sock"
python3 -c 'import socket, sys; socket.socket(socket.AF_UNIX).bind(sys.argv[1])' "$sock"
ask "crashed compositor, socket left behind:"

rm -rf "$rt"
```

```
live compositor, event loop stalled:     exit 6 after 5.2s: Hyprland IPC didn't respond in time  Couldn't read (6) 
crashed compositor, socket left behind:  exit 4 after 0.0s: Couldn't connect to /tmp/tmp.H6OvQ7rYPI/hypr/review_0_0/.socket.sock. (4) 
exit 0
```

If the bind is refused, the slow-resume case is dropped without `skip`, so the `quattro` tip's `./test/shell` does not report it. **Impact:** the regression check can vanish unnoticed.

**Suggested change:** after rebasing, add an `else skip "<reason>"` branch.

<details><summary>More findings</summary>

### A teardown during the wait is logged as a compositor failure

Inside the socket wait, `compositor_alive` returns 1 once `terminating` is set, and the caller then logs "the compositor stopped answering". **Impact:** after a teardown signal that lands during the wait, the journal names the compositor rather than the teardown.

**Suggested change:** put `(( terminating )) && exit 0` as the first line inside `if ! compositor_alive; then`.

**Reproducer (teardown during the wait, at d4b4b75):**

Case below inserted into `test/shell.d/launch-shell-test.sh` at the PR head, just before `# A signal mid-backoff only reaches the trap once the sleep is over.` It reuses the file's own stubs: the fake `hyprctl` misses 1000 queries while the bound socket from the PR's fixture is present, so the launcher is inside the new wait when it gets `SIGTERM`.

```bash
# A session teardown during the socket wait ends supervision promptly.
# Inserted before "# A signal mid-backoff only reaches the trap once the sleep
# is over." in test/shell.d/launch-shell-test.sh.
if (( socket_bound )); then
  : >"$qs_log"
  : >"$qs_env_log"
  : >"$logger_log"
  rm -f "$hyprctl_misses"

  PATH="$fake_bin:$PATH" \
  OMARCHY_PATH="$shell_root" \
  OMARCHY_TEST_QS_LOG="$qs_log" \
  OMARCHY_TEST_QS_ENV_LOG="$qs_env_log" \
  OMARCHY_TEST_QS_STATUSES=$'255\n0' \
  OMARCHY_TEST_COMPOSITOR_GONE=0 \
  OMARCHY_TEST_LOGGER_LOG="$logger_log" \
  OMARCHY_TEST_QS_TERMINATED="$qs_terminated" \
  OMARCHY_TEST_HYPRCTL_MISSES=1000 \
  OMARCHY_TEST_HYPRCTL_MISS_COUNT="$hyprctl_misses" \
  XDG_RUNTIME_DIR="$runtime_dir" \
  HYPRLAND_INSTANCE_SIGNATURE="$signature" \
    "$ROOT/bin/omarchy-launch-shell" &
  launch_pid=$!

  # Past the three quick queries and inside the wait.
  for (( waited = 0; waited < 200; waited++ )); do
    (( $(cat "$hyprctl_misses" 2>/dev/null || echo 0) >= 5 )) && break
    sleep 0.05
  done

  signalled=$SECONDS
  kill -TERM "$launch_pid"
  wait "$launch_pid" || fail "a supervisor signalled during the wait exits cleanly"
  launch_pid=""
  (( SECONDS - signalled <= 2 )) || fail "a teardown during the wait ends supervision promptly" "took $(( SECONDS - signalled ))s"
  [[ $(launches) == 1 ]] || fail "a supervisor signalled during the wait does not relaunch" "$(<"$qs_log")"
  pass "a teardown during the wait ends supervision promptly"

  # Optional wording check: the journal line blames the compositor.
  if [[ ${CHECK_WORDING:-0} == 1 ]]; then
    ! grep -F 'stopped answering' "$logger_log" >/dev/null ||
      fail "a teardown during the wait is not logged as a compositor that stopped answering" "$(<"$logger_log")"
    pass "a teardown during the wait is not logged as a compositor that stopped answering"
  fi
fi
```

### "Up to 30 more seconds" is not a bound

The 30 s is only the sleep budget: against a stand-in for a crashed compositor that left its socket (Hyprland unlinks it only on a clean exit), the head waited 31.4 s, and against a stalled one it was still waiting at 120 s, where the base stood down after 16.4 s. A SIGTERM to the launcher's process group ended the wait in 0.01 s (0.50 s when sent to the launcher alone). **Impact:** the PR text understates how long supervision can continue on a dead or stalled compositor.

**Suggested change:** describe the wait as up to 60 polls rather than 30 s in the PR text.

**Reproducer (launcher timing, base and head):**

Runs `bin/omarchy-launch-shell` from a base checkout (b679363) and a PR-head checkout (d4b4b759) with the real `hyprctl` client (hyprland 0.56.2-2) against two stand-in sockets: *crashed* (bound, nobody listening, what a compositor that aborted leaves behind) and *stalled* (listening with Hyprland's backlog of 10, never accepting, like an event loop that is not running). Quickshell, `logger` and `systemd-cat` are stubs; the first shell exits 255. Needs `python3` and `hyprctl`; private runtime dir only.

```bash
#!/bin/bash
# How long bin/omarchy-launch-shell supervises after the shell dies, against
# stand-in compositor sockets and the real hyprctl client. Quickshell, logger
# and systemd-cat are stubs; the runtime dir is private.
# usage: guard-timing.sh <checkout> [<checkout>...]   (e.g. base and PR head)
set -u
tmp=$(mktemp -d)
sig=review_0_0

mkdir -p "$tmp/bin" "$tmp/root/shell"
cat >"$tmp/bin/quickshell" <<'SH'
#!/bin/bash
echo launch >>"$TMP_QS_LOG"
(( $(wc -l <"$TMP_QS_LOG") == 1 )) && exit 255   # first shell dies like Qt on a broken connection
trap 'exit 143' TERM
while true; do sleep 0.05; done
SH
cat >"$tmp/bin/systemd-cat" <<'SH'
#!/bin/bash
while (( $# > 0 )); do [[ $1 == "--" ]] && { shift; break; }; shift; done
exec "$@"
SH
cat >"$tmp/bin/logger" <<'SH'
#!/bin/bash
shift 2
echo "logger: $*" >>"$TMP_LOGGER_LOG"
SH
cat >"$tmp/bin/hyprctl" <<'SH'
#!/bin/bash
echo query >>"$TMP_HYPRCTL_LOG"
exec /usr/bin/hyprctl "$@"
SH
chmod +x "$tmp/bin"/*

# crashed: a bound socket nobody listens on. stalled: listening (backlog 10, as
# Hyprland), never accepting, like an event loop that is not running.
make_socket() {
  local kind=$1 dir="$tmp/rt-$kind-$RANDOM/hypr/$sig"
  mkdir -p "$dir"
  if [[ $kind == crashed ]]; then
    python3 -c 'import socket, sys; socket.socket(socket.AF_UNIX).bind(sys.argv[1])' "$dir/.socket.sock"
  else
    python3 -c '
import socket, sys, time
s = socket.socket(socket.AF_UNIX); s.bind(sys.argv[1]); s.listen(10)
open(sys.argv[2], "w").write("ready"); time.sleep(3600)
' "$dir/.socket.sock" "$dir/ready" >/dev/null 2>&1 &
    listener=$!
    until [[ -f $dir/ready ]]; do sleep 0.05; done
  fi
  runtime=${dir%/hypr/$sig}
}

run() {  # <checkout> <kind>
  local checkout=$1 kind=$2 start end rc
  listener=""
  make_socket "$kind"
  : >"$tmp/qs.log"; : >"$tmp/logger.log"; : >"$tmp/hyprctl.log"
  start=$(date +%s.%N)
  PATH="$tmp/bin:$PATH" OMARCHY_PATH="$tmp/root" XDG_RUNTIME_DIR="$runtime" \
    HYPRLAND_INSTANCE_SIGNATURE="$sig" TMP_QS_LOG="$tmp/qs.log" \
    TMP_LOGGER_LOG="$tmp/logger.log" TMP_HYPRCTL_LOG="$tmp/hyprctl.log" \
    timeout 120 "$checkout/bin/omarchy-launch-shell"
  rc=$?
  end=$(date +%s.%N)
  [[ -n $listener ]] && { kill "$listener"; wait "$listener" 2>/dev/null; }
  printf '%-8s %-8s exit %-3s after %5.1fs, %2d hyprctl queries, %d launch(es)%s\n' \
    "$(basename "$checkout")" "$kind" "$rc" "$(awk -v a="$start" -v b="$end" 'BEGIN { print b - a }')" \
    "$(wc -l <"$tmp/hyprctl.log")" "$(wc -l <"$tmp/qs.log")" \
    "$( (( rc == 124 )) && echo ', still waiting when timeout 120 stopped it')"
  sed 's/^/         /' "$tmp/logger.log"
}

for checkout in "$@"; do
  run "$checkout" crashed
  run "$checkout" stalled
done
rm -rf "$tmp"
```
